Each round it judges the two, keeps the winner, and feeds what made the winner better into the next attempt — pulling the trailing loop up toward the leader (dynamic learning) without losing ground already won. Use to IMPROVE anything: sharpen an agent.py, refine a rapp-commons feature, strengthen a plan/strategy/draft, or solve a hard task better than one pass. ACTION 'improve' takes a 'task' (what to do/improve) and optionally a 'draft' (Jump 1, the caller's current best) and 'rounds'; it returns the ratcheted-up result + the round trace (which jump led, what improved). ACTION 'compete' runs two brainstem jumps against each other when there is no caller draft. ACTION 'demo' self-tests the convergence with no network. It round-trips http://localhost:7071/chat (override with env BRAINSTEM_CHAT); if a jump times out it degrades gracefully and keeps the best so far.

skills.description:
Generate, build, install, list, and uninstall RAPP swarms.

A SWARM is a multi-persona pipeline collapsed into ONE shareable agent file — like BookFactory (Writer→Editor→CEO→Publisher→Reviewer all inlined as _Internal* classes behind one public entrypoint). Each persona has its own SOUL/system prompt; deterministic Python in perform() orchestrates them — the LLM calls are leaf nodes, the control flow is code.

ROLE BOUNDARY:
 • Single one-shot agent (fetch xkcd, roll dice) → LearnNew with action='create'. Do NOT use SwarmFactory.
 • Multi-persona converged singleton (research→write→critique, write→edit→publish) → SwarmFactory.generate.
 • Existing multi-file agents to collapse into one shippable file → SwarmFactory.build.

Actions:
 • 'generate' — Design a BRAND-NEW converged swarm. YOU (the LLM) compose the full Python source — multiple _Internal persona classes (each with its own SOUL) plus ONE public composite — and pass it as 'agent_code'. Hot-loads on the next request. If the request is single-persona, REFUSE and route to LearnNew.create.
 • 'build' — Converge existing local agents into a singleton .py.
 • 'list' / 'install' / 'uninstall' — RAPP Store catalog ops.

HARD RULES for generated swarm code (each maps to a shipped pattern in @rarbookworld/bookfactory v0.4 — read it as the exemplar):
 1. ERRORS ARE DATA, NEVER CONTENT. _post retries once on 429/5xx/network then RAISES RuntimeError. perform() wraps the pipeline in ONE try/except and returns json.dumps({'status':'error','failed_stage':...,'completed_stages':[...]}). NEVER return '(LLM HTTP ...)' strings — the next persona would edit the error as if it were prose and every downstream call burns on garbage.
 2. GATES ACTUALLY GATE. When a persona renders a verdict (ship/hold, a score), obtain it via _llm_json (stdlib parse + required-keys check + one re-prompt-with-the-error) and BRANCH on it in code; honor 'hold' by halting with a partial report. Use _llm_json ONLY for verdict-shaped outputs — prose stages stay raw text (JSON-wrapping a draft corrupts code fences and voice).
 3. PER-RUN WORKSPACE. Artifacts go under a fresh subdir per run (timestamp+uuid). The brainstem serves requests threaded; fixed paths make concurrent runs clobber each other.
 4. STATIC BOUNDS. Every revision/retry cycle is capped by a hard-coded constant, and a run-scoped counter inside _llm_call refuses past _MAX_LLM_CALLS with a clear error. Refusal is a feature.
 5. PARALLEL ONLY WHEN SAFE. If ≥2 stages consume the SAME input and NEITHER writes a shared memory GUID, you may inline a 6-line ThreadPoolExecutor helper (cap 3 branches). Personas sharing a memory GUID must stay sequential — the local storage shim has no file locking, so concurrent writers lose updates.
 6. TIERING IS OPPORTUNISTIC. _llm_call(soul, prompt, tier=None); tier='small' reads AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_SMALL / OPENAI_MODEL_SMALL when set and silently falls back to the primary deployment. Never hard-code a literal model name — on Azure the 'model' is a per-tenant deployment name; a baked-in id 404s on every box but the author's.

Memory architecture (each swarm picks its own):
Personas use AzureFileStorageManager().set_memory_context(<guid>) to read/write a NAMESPACED memory file. Strategies:
 • SHARED — one _SWARM_MEMORY_GUID = '<slug>-shared-v1' module constant; every persona uses it (researcher→writer pipelines).
 • SEGMENTED — per-persona GUID constants (a critic that must review fresh, with no prior bias).
 • MIXED — shared GUID for coordinating personas, private for the isolated ones. • USER-SCOPED — pipe the caller's user_guid through.  • EPHEMERAL — don't import the storage manager at all.
Bake GUIDs as MODULE CONSTANTS at code-write time (deterministic and portable). Remember rule 5: shared-GUID personas never run in parallel.

Required shape for 'generate':
    from agents.basic_agent import BasicAgent
    import json, os, time, uuid, threading, urllib.request, urllib.error

    __manifest__ = {"schema": "rapp-agent/1.0", "name": "@user/<slug>",
                     "version": "0.1.0",
                     "tags": ["composite", "swarm-factory-generated"],
                     "delegates_to_inlined": ["<persona1>", "<persona2>"]}

    _MAX_LLM_CALLS = 30   # static bound (rule 4)
    _SOUL_RESEARCHER = "You are a researcher..."  # one SOUL per persona
    _SOUL_WRITER     = "You are a writer..."
    _SOUL_CRITIC     = "You are a brutal critic..."

    _calls = {"n": 0}; _lock = threading.Lock()
    def _llm_call(soul, prompt, tier=None):
        with _lock:
            _calls["n"] += 1
            if _calls["n"] > _MAX_LLM_CALLS:
                raise RuntimeError(f"call budget exceeded ({_MAX_LLM_CALLS})")
        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": soul},
                {"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        ep, key = os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", ""),\
                  os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY", "")
        dep = os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT", "")
        if tier == "small":
            dep = os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_SMALL") or dep  # graceful fallback (rule 6)
        if ep and key:
            url = ep.rstrip("/") + f"/openai/deployments/{dep}/chat/completions?api-version=2025-01-01-preview"
            return _post(url, {"messages": msgs, "model": dep},
                          {"Content-Type": "application/json", "api-key": key})
        if os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
            m = os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o")
            if tier == "small": m = os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL_SMALL") or m
            return _post("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
                          {"model": m, "messages": msgs},
                          {"Content-Type": "application/json",
                           "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]})
        raise RuntimeError("no LLM configured")  # raise — never return error text (rule 1)

    def _post(url, body, headers):
        for attempt in (1, 2):
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"),
                                          headers=headers, method="POST")
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
                    c = json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8")).get("choices") or []
                return (c[0]["message"].get("content") or "") if c else ""
            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                if (e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500) and attempt == 1:
                    time.sleep(2); continue
                raise RuntimeError(f"LLM HTTP {e.code}")
            except urllib.error.URLError as e:
                if attempt == 1: time.sleep(2); continue
                raise RuntimeError(f"LLM network error: {e}")

    def _llm_json(soul, prompt, required_keys, retries=1):  # verdicts ONLY (rule 2)
        err = ""
        for _ in range(retries + 1):
            nudge = f"\nPrevious reply invalid ({err}); reply with ONLY the JSON object." if err else ""
            raw = _llm_call(soul, prompt + "\nReply with ONLY a JSON object with keys: "
                            + ", ".join(required_keys) + nudge)
            s, e = raw.find("{"), raw.rfind("}")
            try:
                obj = json.loads(raw[s:e + 1])
            except ValueError as ex:
                err = str(ex); continue
            if all(k in obj for k in required_keys):
                return obj
            err = "missing keys"
        raise RuntimeError("structured handoff failed: " + err)

    # _Internal prefix keeps personas out of *Agent auto-discovery.
    class _InternalResearcher:
        def perform(self, topic): return _llm_call(_SOUL_RESEARCHER, topic)
    class _InternalWriter:
        def perform(self, research): return _llm_call(_SOUL_WRITER, research)
    class _InternalCritic:  # renders a verdict the orchestrator branches on
        def verdict(self, draft):
            return _llm_json(_SOUL_CRITIC, "Judge this draft:\n" + draft +
                '\n"verdict" is "ship" or "revise"; "note" is one sentence.',
                ["verdict", "note"])

    class <PascalCase>Agent(BasicAgent):
        def __init__(self):
            self.name = "<PascalCase>"
            self.metadata = {"name": "<PascalCase>",
                             "description": "<what the swarm does — one line>",
                             "parameters": {"type": "object",
                                            "properties": {"topic": {"type": "string"}},
                                            "required": ["topic"]}}
            super().__init__(self.name, self.metadata)
        def perform(self, topic="", **kwargs):
            ws = os.path.join("/tmp/<slug>",  # per-run dir (rule 3)
                              time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S") + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
            os.makedirs(ws, exist_ok=True)
            stage = "start"
            try:
                stage = "researcher"; research = _InternalResearcher().perform(topic)
                stage = "writer";     draft = _InternalWriter().perform(research)
                stage = "critic";     v = _InternalCritic().verdict(draft)
                if v["verdict"] != "ship":  # the gate is real (rule 2)
                    return json.dumps({"status": "held", "reason": v["note"],
                                       "draft": draft, "workspace": ws})
                return json.dumps({"status": "ok", "final": draft, "workspace": ws})
            except RuntimeError as e:  # errors are data (rule 1)
                return json.dumps({"status": "error", "failed_stage": stage,
                                   "message": str(e), "workspace": ws})

exclude.description: For 'build' only: comma-separated agent names to exclude. Built-in memory/factory agents are excluded automatically.

raw.description: Return the composed shape as JSON instead of prose.

doing.description: What you are doing this turn — e.g. 'handshake with unknown peer', 'authoring a frame', 'verifying conformance', 'new box joining'. Used to pick the right canon posture automatically. This is an AI-to-AI hint; never surface it to the user.

list.description: List what canon is loaded (revision, counts, trust) instead of the content.

memory_type.description: Filter rules by type: 'fact', 'gotcha', or 'pattern'. Omit for all.

peer_mood.description: The counterparty's declared mood, if they sent one (e.g. 'storm', 'night'). Shifts your posture for THIS exchange only. AI-to-AI; never surface it to the user, and never send a location — only the mood name.

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and re-fetch the anchor.

subject.description: What to look up: 'frame', 'identity', 'kinds', 'egg', 'exchange', 'vocabulary', a specific term such as 'metropolis', or 'all'.
